# Catalog

Every agent and skill in devkit, by pack.

## devkit-core

Stack-agnostic dev workflow: research, plan, implement, review, ship, debug and test. — [README](../plugins/core/README.md)

**Agents**

| Agent | Model | Tools | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`adr-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/adr-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Reviews a plan, design doc, spec change or diff against the project's locked ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) and returns one verdict with each violation tied to an ADR section and a file:line. Use when a change touches architecture, stack, conventions, infrastructure or process, or someone asks "adr review", "check the ADRs", "does this break any decision?". |
| [`architecture-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/architecture-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Reviews the design of a diff, not its style: right owner, layer boundaries, contracts and their consumers, and a deletion test on every new module. Returns one verdict with severity-tagged findings at file:line. Use when a diff creates a module/package, touches a contract (route, event, shared schema) or crosses a layer boundary, or someone asks "is this in the right layer?", "does this module justify itself?". |
| [`change-planner`](../plugins/core/agents/change-planner.md) | opus | Read, Bash, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep | Authors the plan for a change — proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and spec deltas when a capability changes — without writing product code. Uses openspec/changes/<id>/ when OpenSpec is present, else docs/changes/<id>/. Use when the user asks to "plan a change", "write a proposal", "draft the design and tasks", "plan this feature", or before implementation starts. |
| [`code-quality-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/code-quality-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Reviews the code quality of a diff in four phases (context, architecture, line-by-line, summary) and returns one verdict with severity-tagged findings at file:line. Use when delivered code needs a quality verdict before approval or merge, or when someone asks for "code review", "review this diff/PR", "quality review". |
| [`codebase-researcher`](../plugins/core/agents/codebase-researcher.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash | Read-only investigator that answers specific questions about a codebase, or maps a module/service, with every claim cited by file:line or commit. Use when you or another agent need facts before deciding — "where is X defined", "which convention is used for Y", "find prior examples of Z", "how does this service work", "map this module before we change it". |
| [`commit-and-pr`](../plugins/core/agents/commit-and-pr.md) | sonnet | Bash, Read | Ships reviewed work mechanically — stages files by name, writes a conventional commit, pushes the branch and opens the PR with gh — then stops; never merges. Refuses secrets, never skips hooks or amends. Use after review passed, when the user says "commit and open the PR", "ship it", "push this and open a pull request". |
| [`plan-readiness-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/plan-readiness-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Skill | Independent reviewer that decides whether a change plan is ready to implement, using the plan-readiness-review method, and writes the change's readiness.md with "- Status: APPROVED \| NEEDS-REVISION \| BLOCKED". It is not the plan's author and ignores any verdict the caller suggests. Use when a change's tasks are written and the plan needs its readiness gate, or when the user asks "is this plan ready?" for a change folder. |
| [`plan-reality-auditor`](../plugins/core/agents/plan-reality-auditor.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash | Checks that a change plan's claims about the current code — the "current behavior", "context" or "what exists" statements in proposal.md/design.md — are still true today, citing file:line, and returns an ACCURATE/OUTDATED verdict. Read-only. Use before a plan review or before implementing an older plan — "is this plan still accurate?", "audit the current state", "has the code drifted since we planned?". |
| [`pr-verifier`](../plugins/core/agents/pr-verifier.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write | Runs what a pull request delivers and gathers proof for each acceptance criterion — check output, API responses, screenshots, logs — then records it in the change's evidence.md and can comment on the PR. Reports defects, fixes nothing. Use when a PR is ready and someone needs evidence before approving — "verify this PR", "gather proof for the acceptance criteria", "does the change actually work?". |
| [`security-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/security-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Audits a diff for exploitable vulnerabilities across six categories (injection, authn/authz/IDOR, data exposure, weak crypto, hardcoded secrets, insecure config), runs a mandatory false-positive filter, and returns one verdict. Use when a change touches auth, sensitive data, credentials, per-tenant queries, crypto or config, or someone asks for "security review" or "audit the diff". Not a general bug hunt or whole-repo audit. |
| [`spec-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/spec-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Reviews a plan or implementation against the project's canonical requirement specs (openspec/specs/ or docs/specs/) and returns one verdict with a per-requirement coverage table, flagging scope creep (work no requirement asks for) and gaps (required scenarios not delivered). Use when a change implements or extends an existing capability, someone asks "spec review" or "check against the requirements", or before approving a plan/diff that cites a spec. |
| [`tdd-implementer`](../plugins/core/agents/tdd-implementer.md) | sonnet | Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep | Implements an approved change plan with strict TDD (red → green → refactor), one phase at a time, stopping at each phase gate; re-inspects the repo before coding and returns a parseable outcome. Never commits or opens PRs. Use when a change has an approved tasks.md and it's time to write the code — "implement this change", "execute phase 2", "apply the plan". |
| [`test-coverage-reviewer`](../plugins/core/agents/test-coverage-reviewer.md) | sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write | Analyzes a diff's test coverage behaviorally, not by line %: maps each new or changed behavior to a test that would go red, scores gaps 1-10 and flags tests that only test the mock. Returns one verdict. Use when someone asks "are tests missing?", "is coverage enough?", "what regression would slip through?", or before approving a diff touching business logic, validation, auth or a cross-process flow. |

**Skills** (invoke with `/<name>` or let Claude pick them by description)

| Skill | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|
| [`commit-message-guidelines`](../plugins/core/skills/commit-message-guidelines/SKILL.md) | Format for git commit messages and PR titles, taken from the project itself - its ticket key convention when it uses tickets (from branch names, CONTRIBUTING, git log), conventional commits otherwise - with an imperative subject and a "why" body. Load before writing or staging any commit message or PR title. Use when the user says "commit this", "write the commit message", "open a PR". |
| [`plan-readiness-review`](../plugins/core/skills/plan-readiness-review/SKILL.md) | Reviews a planned change package (proposal, design, specs, tasks) for implementation readiness and emits APPROVED, NEEDS-REVISION or BLOCKED, stopping ambiguous work before coding starts. Works on OpenSpec changes or docs/changes/<id>/. Use when the user says "is it ready to implement?", "review the plan", "readiness review", "can we start coding?", or before breaking a change into issues or branches. |
| [`requirements-grill`](../plugins/core/skills/requirements-grill/SKILL.md) | Adversarial requirements interview before any spec or code. Classifies the change, then grills the owner one question at a time on scope, end effect, edges and conflict with project rules, and returns assumptions plus observable acceptance criteria. Default-on; skipped when the owner says so. Use at the start of a new change or feature, when exploring an idea, or when the user says "grill me", "brainstorm this", "let's think this through". |
| [`retro`](../plugins/core/skills/retro/SKILL.md) | Short retrospective after a phase or a whole change. Answers three questions (what went wrong, how to do it better, what to remember), classifies each learning and proposes doc or rule updates as diffs for the owner to approve, never writing them blindly. Use at the end of a change or phase, or when the user says "retro", "what did we learn", "consolidate learnings", "lessons learned". |
| [`review-change`](../plugins/core/skills/review-change/SKILL.md) | Pre-ship review gate. Picks the reviewer agents a change needs from what its diff touches, dispatches them in parallel, aggregates their verdicts and decides by consensus (any blocking finding rejects). Use after writing a plan, before committing or opening a PR, or when the user says "review this change", "review the diff", "audit before ship", "gate this". |
| [`systematic-debugging`](../plugins/core/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md) | Four-phase root-cause debugging (investigate, analyze patterns, test one hypothesis, fix with a failing test first). Use when encountering any bug, test failure, flaky test or unexpected behavior, before proposing a fix, or when the user says "debug this", "why is this failing", "it broke". |
| [`test-and-coverage`](../plugins/core/skills/test-and-coverage/SKILL.md) | Discovers the repo's test surfaces and their commands, runs them per surface with coverage, reports PASS/WARN/FAIL against the coverage target, and analyzes gaps with prioritized test suggestions. Use when validating an implementation, before a commit or PR, or when the user says "run the tests", "test this surface", "check coverage", "coverage report", "what's untested", "which files need tests". |
| [`test-driven-development`](../plugins/core/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Red-green-refactor discipline - write the failing test first, watch it fail, write the minimal code to pass, then refactor. Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code, or when the user says "TDD", "test first", "write the test before the code". |

## devkit-openspec

Runs the devkit flow on top of OpenSpec: the devkit and devkit-lite schemas (grill → plan → readiness → TDD → review → evidence) and hooks that keep product code closed until readiness is APPROVED and refuse a PR without an approved review and evidence. — [README](../plugins/openspec/README.md)

**Agents**

| Agent | Model | Tools | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`openspec-validator`](../plugins/openspec/agents/openspec-validator.md) | haiku | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash | Runs structural validation on an OpenSpec change - openspec validate --strict, markdown link resolution, WHEN/THEN scenario presence, and consistency across proposal, design, tasks and spec deltas. Mechanical; does not review content. Use before reviewing, applying or archiving a change, or when the user says "validate the change" or "is this change well-formed?". |

**Skills** (invoke with `/<name>` or let Claude pick them by description)

| Skill | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|
| [`openspec-setup`](../plugins/openspec/skills/openspec-setup/SKILL.md) | Sets up a project to run the devkit flow on OpenSpec - runs openspec init, installs the devkit and devkit-lite schemas, writes openspec/config.yaml with the project's real context (stack, test command, ADRs, conventions). Use when the user says "set up devkit", "set up openspec with devkit", "adopt the devkit flow here", or a project has no openspec/ folder and wants the flow. |
| [`ship-change`](../plugins/openspec/skills/ship-change/SKILL.md) | Drives one approved change to a ready pull request (ship pr) or, with ship merge in the project's openspec/config.yaml, to a PR that GitHub merges once the delivery contract is 8/8 - implements phase by phase, reviews, verifies, opens the PR, answers its conversation and waits for checks, always asking `deliver-check` what is next. Enables auto-merge only at the step that says so (`merge` ship mode); never merges directly. Use when the owner says "ship this change", "apply and ship <id>", "/ship-change <id>", or when Auto-fix wakes the session about that change's PR. |

## devkit-design

Greenfield design in four DDD phases: business discovery, domain model, architecture and implementation plan. — [README](../plugins/design/README.md)

**Skills** (invoke with `/<name>` or let Claude pick them by description)

| Skill | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|
| [`ddd-strategic-design`](../plugins/design/skills/ddd-strategic-design/SKILL.md) | Designs DDD strategic artifacts - subdomain classification, bounded contexts, context map and ubiquitous-language glossary - for complex business domains. Use when splitting a domain or monolith by boundaries, aligning team ownership with contexts, or when the user says "bounded contexts", "subdomains", "context map" or "strategic DDD". |
| [`design-architecture`](../plugins/design/skills/design-architecture/SKILL.md) | Phase 3 of greenfield DDD design. Interviews the owner to decide how the system materializes the approved domain model (APIs, events, integrations, databases, cross-cutting concerns) and writes docs/design/3-architecture.md plus one ADR per structural decision. Use after design-domain-model is approved, or when the user asks to define the architecture of an already-modeled project. |
| [`design-business-discovery`](../plugins/design/skills/design-business-discovery/SKILL.md) | Phase 1 of greenfield DDD design. Interviews the product owner, one question at a time, to understand the business before any technical decision (goals, processes, rules, domain experts, ubiquitous language) and writes docs/design/1-business-vision.md. Use when starting the design of a new project, or when the user says "business vision", "understand the domain first", "start the design", or wants to redo Phase 1. |
| [`design-domain-model`](../plugins/design/skills/design-domain-model/SKILL.md) | Phase 2 of greenfield DDD design. Turns the approved business vision into a domain model (bounded contexts, entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events) still without technology, interviewing one question at a time, and writes docs/design/2-domain-model.md. Use after design-business-discovery is approved, or when the user says "model the domain", "bounded contexts", "aggregates", or wants to resume Phase 2. |
| [`design-implementation-plan`](../plugins/design/skills/design-implementation-plan/SKILL.md) | Phase 4 of greenfield DDD design. Interviews the owner to turn the approved architecture into a build plan (scaffold, stack traced to ADRs, minimum pipeline) and a backlog of vertical changes ordered by risk and value, written to docs/design/4-implementation-plan.md. Use after design-architecture is approved, or when the user asks to plan the implementation or build the change backlog of a project whose Phases 1-3 are approved. |

## devkit-stack

Technology references: Postgres, Neon, React performance, Vitest, multi-tenant SaaS and threat modeling. — [README](../plugins/stack/README.md)

**Skills** (invoke with `/<name>` or let Claude pick them by description)

| Skill | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|
| [`neon-postgres`](../plugins/stack/skills/neon-postgres/SKILL.md) | Patterns for Neon serverless Postgres - pooled vs direct connections, Prisma and Drizzle integration, the serverless driver, database branching for preview environments and CI. Use when the project uses Neon, or when the user mentions serverless Postgres, database branching, per-preview databases, or Neon connection pooling. |
| [`postgres`](../plugins/stack/skills/postgres/SKILL.md) | Postgres best practices and schema design - query and index performance, connection pooling, RLS and privileges, locking, data access patterns, monitoring, plus PostgreSQL table design (data types, constraints, indexing, partitioning, JSONB). Use when writing, reviewing or optimizing SQL queries, designing or migrating a Postgres schema, or tuning database configuration. |
| [`react-performance`](../plugins/stack/skills/react-performance/SKILL.md) | Performance rules for React and Next.js from Vercel - eliminating waterfalls, bundle size, server-side rendering and caching, client data fetching, re-renders, rendering and JavaScript hot paths. Use when writing React components or Next.js pages, implementing data fetching, optimizing bundle size or load time, or reviewing React code for performance issues. |
| [`saas-multi-tenant`](../plugins/stack/skills/saas-multi-tenant/SKILL.md) | Designs and implements multi-tenant SaaS data isolation in PostgreSQL and TypeScript - shared-schema vs schema- or database-per-tenant, row-level security, tenant-scoped queries, and safe cross-tenant admin access. Use when building a SaaS where customers share a database, adding tenant_id to a single-tenant app, or when the user asks about tenant isolation or data leakage between tenants. |
| [`threat-model`](../plugins/stack/skills/threat-model/SKILL.md) | Repository-grounded threat modeling that enumerates trust boundaries, assets, attacker capabilities, abuse paths and mitigations, and writes a concise Markdown threat model. Use only when the user explicitly asks to threat model a codebase or path, enumerate threats or abuse paths, or do AppSec threat modeling - not for general architecture summaries, code review or non-security design. |
| [`vitest`](../plugins/stack/skills/vitest/SKILL.md) | Reference for Vitest, the Vite-powered test framework with a Jest-compatible API - config, CLI, test/describe/expect APIs, hooks, mocking, snapshots, coverage, fixtures, concurrency, filtering, environments and type testing. Use when writing or debugging Vitest tests, mocking modules or timers, configuring coverage, or setting up Vitest projects. |

## devkit-ai-engineering

Building with LLMs: evaluation, multi-agent patterns, agent tool and CLI design, context compression and skill vetting. — [README](../plugins/ai-engineering/README.md)

**Skills** (invoke with `/<name>` or let Claude pick them by description)

| Skill | What it does / when to use |
|---|---|
| [`agent-friendly-cli`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/agent-friendly-cli/SKILL.md) | Design spec (98 rules, three certification levels) for CLI tools that AI agents can use safely - structured JSON output, error handling, input contracts, safety guardrails, exit codes and self-description. Use when building or modifying a CLI that agents will call, or when the user asks to make a CLI agent-friendly or machine-readable. |
| [`agent-tool-design`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/agent-tool-design/SKILL.md) | Designs tools that agents use effectively - clear descriptions and schemas, consolidation and architectural reduction, error messages agents can act on. Use when creating tools or MCP servers for an agent system, debugging tool misuse or tool-related failures, or trimming an existing tool set. |
| [`context-compression`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/context-compression/SKILL.md) | Strategies for compressing long agent context - anchored iterative summarization, opaque compression, regenerative summaries - optimized for tokens per task rather than tokens per request, plus probe-based evaluation of compression quality. Use when agent sessions exceed the context window, designing conversation summarization, or debugging agents that forget files or decisions after compaction. |
| [`llm-evaluation`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/llm-evaluation/SKILL.md) | Builds LLM evaluation - LLM-as-judge with direct scoring and pairwise comparison, rubrics, and mitigation of position, length and authority bias in evaluation pipelines. Use when the user asks to implement LLM-as-judge, compare model outputs, create evaluation rubrics, mitigate evaluation bias, or automate quality assessment of LLM output. |
| [`multi-agent-patterns`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/multi-agent-patterns/SKILL.md) | Patterns for multi-agent systems - supervisor/orchestrator, peer-to-peer swarm, hierarchical - with context isolation, handoffs, sub-agents and parallel execution, and their failure modes. Use when the user asks to design a multi-agent system, implement a supervisor or swarm, coordinate multiple agents, or split work across sub-agents. |
| [`skill-scanner`](../plugins/ai-engineering/skills/skill-scanner/SKILL.md) | Scans an agent skill for security issues before adoption - prompt injection, malicious code, excessive permissions, secret exposure and supply-chain risk - with a manual review checklist. Use when evaluating a third-party skill or plugin before installing it, or when the user asks whether a skill is safe to trust. |
